messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The test `testOptionGroupLong` fails because the `OptionGroup` class does not properly handle selection of options that have a long name but no short name (i.e., their "opt" string is null). The test sets up an `OptionGroup` containing two options, both created with only a long option name (`withLongOpt("foo")`, `withLongOpt("bar")`). Since no short option names are provided, when the parser parses `--bar`, the `OptionGroup` should mark "bar" as selected.

Looking at the code of `OptionGroup.setSelected(Option option)`, it uses `option.getOpt()` to store and compare the selected option. However, in this case, `option.getOpt()` returns null since no short option (`opt`) was set during option creation (only `longOpt` was set). The method logic checks whether `selected == null || selected.equals(option.getOpt())`, but since `option.getOpt()` is null, and `selected` is also null initially, it sets `selected = option.getOpt()` which is null.

Thus, when later calling `group.getSelected()`, `selected` is null, failing the assertion in the test `assertEquals("selected option", "bar", group.getSelected());`.

This shows that `OptionGroup` only considers short option names (opt) for selection tracking, and ignores or does not support purely long options with no short name. The group selection tracking relies on `option.getOpt()` strings, which are null for long-only options created via `OptionBuilder.withLongOpt()` without specifying a short opt.

In summary, the root cause is that `OptionGroup.setSelected()` and the related selection logic handles option identification only through `option.getOpt()` (short option), missing or ignoring long option names. Options created with only a long name have `opt == null`. Therefore, methods like `setSelected()` silently fail to mark them as selected.

Recent bug reports and the current bug report confirm this issue is specific to long-only options in groups, matching the failure scenario seen in the test.

Hence, the failure occurs because `OptionGroup` does not correctly handle option selection for options where `getOpt()` is null, and it should be extended to consider and store long option names as well for pure long options.

Suggested fix location: `OptionGroup.setSelected(Option)` and possibly related methods that handle option selection and tracking within `OptionGroup`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
